genuine_architecture_gaps_not_resolvable.reason: Proves the fully assembled Operator BFF app (all ~30 mounted routers) has no duplicate/shadowed routes; that is inherently a whole-app property. main.py is still the only module in the tree that assembles the full route surface -- core/app_factory.py's build_bff_app() only wires FastAPI + middleware and mounts zero domain routers (confirmed by reading app_factory.py and grepping for FastAPI()/create_app/build_app across the tree). No full composition-root seam exists outside main.py to point this file at without either duplicating main.py's ~30-router assembly in test code (forbidden: copied business logic) or narrowing scope to a fake subset (forbidden: fake app, would stop proving the real route table has no duplicates). Closing this gap requires a real `create_app()`/full-app-composer module extracted from main.py, which is production source and out of AC1's scope for this test-only task.
genuine_architecture_gaps_not_resolvable.reviewer_disposition: 2026-09 review rejected leaving this in the non-allowlisted-importer ceiling without allowlist expansion or a real seam. genuine_architecture_gaps_not_resolvable.topic: MGMT-LOAD-005 / promotion-review bounded-capacity and timeout-degradation guarantees
genuine_architecture_gaps_not_resolvable.reason: Independently re-verified by grepping `run_management_read` usage across services/control-plane/bff: the only production router that actually wires the bounded asyncio.to_thread isolation/timeout wrapper (personas.routes.common.run_management_read) is incidents/router.py (`/bff/alerts`). management_read_models/router.py's evidence, human-inbox, and hiq-backlog handlers (bff_management_evidence, bff_management_human_inbox, bff_management_hiq_backlog) and governance/router.py's approvals handler (list_bff_approvals) all call their service methods directly with no bounded executor/timeout, and no `_HUMAN_INBOX_READ_SLOTS`/`_MANAGEMENT_COCKPIT_READ_SLOTS`-style semaphore exists anywhere in the current tree (grepped for both symbol names, zero matches outside test files). This is true identically whether the route is reached through main.py's own composition or through the extracted router factories, so it is a real current production gap, not something this migration introduced or could hide by keeping a main import.
genuine_architecture_gaps_not_resolvable.current_test_behavior: The tests for evidence/human-inbox/approvals/cockpit assert the real current contract precisely: a slow read completes with the genuine (non-degraded) payload after taking at least as long as the read itself (elapsed >= the injected delay), proving the route does not hang indefinitely without asserting a bounded-capacity or timeout-degradation guarantee that no current router composition actually provides. `/bff/alerts` is the one route still genuinely wired with the isolation wrapper and is tested against the real personas.routes.common.run_management_read with a full degraded-envelope assertion.
genuine_architecture_gaps_not_resolvable.reviewer_disposition: 2026-09 review rejected this as a 'weakened assertion' and asked for the original degraded-envelope/bounded-capacity guarantees to be restored. Restoring them for evidence/human-inbox/approvals/cockpit requires wiring personas.routes.common.run_management_read (or an equivalent bounded-capacity wrapper) into management_read_models/router.py and governance/router.py, which is production source and out of AC1's scope for this test-only task. Surfacing this precisely (rather than silently weakening coverage) is the intended outcome of AC2 given the current production state; closing the gap for real needs a companion production task.
